class.name: GroundSurface3D
class.brief_description: Footprints, ruts and dents in sand, soil, mud and leaf litter.
class.description: A field of dents and rims around the camera over bare ground. Nodes in [member deform_groups] press it: loaded bodies sink by Bekker's pressure-sinkage relation with Wong's soil values ([i]Theory of Ground Vehicles[/i]), the pressed material is partly compacted and partly pushed into a rim so volume is kept, and walls steeper than the material's angle of repose slump down (Sumner, O'Brien and Hodgins 1999, "Animating Sand, Mud, and Snow"). What the ground is made of follows rules per place: [member ground_type] (or [member type_map]) gives sand or soil; the moisture ([member moisture], or the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wetness) turns soil to mud and dry sand to damp sand, so a boot sinks 2 cm in dry sand, under 1 cm in damp sand and about 8 cm in mud, dry sand prints cave in to dishes, damp ones keep sharp walls and mud creeps back over minutes; tree crowns (the weather map's canopy closure) drop [member litter_depth] of leaf litter; bare rock from a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code] height source does not print, nor does ground under a [code]SnowCover3D[/code] pack. Freshly turned ground is darker until it dries ([member drying_time]); wind fills dry sand prints and rain softens them. The node draws the field as a patch with [member material], the terrain's own material, and the terrain drawn with that material (with [member BaseMaterial3D.ground_deform_enabled], or [method BaseMaterial3D.get_ground_deform_shader_code] in a shader) is lowered under the patch by [member skirt], so the prints are geometry in raster and under path tracing. Bodies keep standing on the terrain's own collider; [method get_surface_height_at] gives the printed surface for foot placement.

method.name: add_wader
method.description: Tells the standing water a tyre centred on [param axle] is moving through it this physics frame at [param velocity] ([param id] names the tyre: a later call with the same id moves it): the water cannot stand inside it, so it is pushed out ahead of it and closes in behind, volume kept, running off as a bow wave and a wake. [PhysXVehicle3D] calls it for its wheels in water. Up to four tyres over the field count.

method.name: add_water
method.description: Adds [param volume] m³ of standing water spread evenly over a disc of [param radius] at [param position], or takes it where [param volume] is negative (thrown spray landing, and water a tyre throws up). Applied by the next water step on the GPU, the disc's area counted in the field's own texels, so the volume is exact. A take that finds less water than it asks for is owed (see [method get_water_owed]) and paid back by the next water added. Added water carries [param mud] kg/m³ of clay (see [member muddy_water]); a take carries off the clay of the water it takes.

method.name: bed_load
method.description: The bed load of fine sand (0.25 mm) under water flowing at [param water_speed] m/s (depth-averaged), m² per second per metre across the flow: Meyer-Peter and Mueller (1948). [code]0.0[/code] under the Shields threshold, about 0.25 m/s.

method.name: bed_load_shear
method.description: The bed load of fine sand (0.25 mm) under a bed shear stress of [param shear_stress] Pa, m² per second per metre across the flow: Meyer-Peter and Mueller (1948). [code]0.0[/code] under the Shields threshold, about 0.19 Pa. Runoff takes its shear from the sheet of water, rho g h S.

method.name: clear_deformation
method.description: Removes every print, including the cached tiles.

method.name: clear_saved_ruts
method.description: Deletes every kept rut tile in [member ruts_path] (see [member keep_ruts]), for a new game or a reset world.

method.name: deposit
method.description: Lays [param depth] m of sand over a disc of [param radius] at [param position] (a hollow there fills first). The volume is the disc's exactly, also for a disc smaller than a cell. Returns it, m3 ([code]0[/code] off soft ground). For grains landing ([PhysXGroundGrains3D]).

method.name: dig
method.description: Takes [param depth] m of sand out of a disc of [param radius] at [param position], any rim there first. Returns the volume, m3 ([code]0[/code] off soft ground). For grains leaving the ground ([PhysXGroundGrains3D]).

method.name: get_blown_at
method.description: The share of the sand at world [param x], [param z] the wind can move (0 to 1): dry sand on open ground 1; damp sand, litter and sand sheltered by plants ([member wind_shelters]) less.

method.name: get_cached_tile_count
method.description: The number of tiles of prints kept for when the field comes back over them.

method.name: get_deform_rect
method.description: The field's world XZ rectangle.

method.name: get_crack_at
method.description: The desiccation cracks at [param position] (see [member desiccation_cracks]): how far open they are (0 to 1), the plate size in metres, how regular the pattern has grown (0 to 1) and how dry the crust is (0 to 1), or, negative, how damp the drying layer still is (to -1).

method.name: get_dent_at
method.description: How far the ground at [param position] is pressed below its undisturbed height, in metres.

method.name: get_deposition_rate_at
method.description: How fast wind-blown sand is piling up at [param position], in m/s (negative where the wind is taking it away): where the saltation flux falls, among plants ([member wind_shelters]) or onto damp sand, the sand it carried lands. A gale over a grass tuft piles about 2 cm an hour on its windward edge.

method.name: get_footing_at
method.description: The footing at [param position] for a walker of [param mass] kg on [param area] m² of boot: [code]soft[/code], [code]sinkage[/code] (m), [code]effort[/code] (the work of walking against firm ground, 2.1 on dry sand), [code]speed_scale[/code] (its inverse) and [code]slide[/code] (an acceleration down a face steeper than the material holds, m/s²). The game decides how a controller uses them.

method.name: get_fresh_at
method.description: How freshly turned the ground at [param position] is, from 1 (just dug) to 0 (dried).

method.name: get_ground_height_at
method.description: The undisturbed ground height at [param position], from the height source.

method.name: get_height
method.description: Same as [method get_surface_height_at], under the name height sources share, so a [PhysXFlow3D]'s [code]terrain_path[/code] can point at this node and its gas rest on the ruts and berms.

method.name: get_material_at
method.description: The rules at [param position]: [code]n[/code], [code]kc[/code], [code]kphi[/code] (Bekker), [code]rim_share[/code], [code]repose[/code] (degrees), [code]rate[/code] (slumping share per second), [code]max_dent[/code], [code]litter[/code] (m), [code]sand[/code] (share), [code]blown[/code] (the share the wind moves: dry, bare sand) and [code]deformable[/code].

method.name: get_moved_volume
method.description: The volume pressed down (x) and piled into rims (y) over the live field, in m³. Their difference is what was compacted.

method.name: get_mud_color_at
method.description: The clay's colour at [param position]: [member mud_color_map] where it covers [member mud_map_rect], else [member mud_color].

method.name: get_mud_depth_at
method.description: The depth of the soft mud layer at [param position], in metres (0 where the ground is not mud or not wet enough; see [member mud_layer]).

method.name: get_near_moved_volume
method.description: As [method get_moved_volume], over the near field ([member near_field]); zero when it is not active.

method.name: get_near_rect
method.description: The near field's square in world XZ, or an empty rect when it is not active.

method.name: get_patch_material
method.description: The copy of [member material] the patch is drawn with.

method.name: get_rim_at
method.description: How much material is piled on the ground at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_ripple_at
method.description: The wind ripple height at [param position] over the ripple layer's mean, in metres; [code]0.0[/code] outside the ripple window or with [member wind_ripples] off.

method.name: get_ripple_cell
method.description: The ripple layer's cell size in metres: [member detail_spacing] divided down to about 1.25 cm, so the patch's fine vertices sit on its cells.

method.name: get_ripple_heights
method.description: The ripple layer's heights, [method get_ripple_size] squared, row by row along Z from [method get_ripple_origin]. For tests and tools.

method.name: get_ripple_origin
method.description: The world XZ of the ripple window's corner, in metres.

method.name: get_ripple_size
method.description: The ripple window's width in cells (it spans [member ripple_extent]).

method.name: get_ripple_steps
method.description: How many saltation steps the ripples have taken since [member wind_ripples] was turned on, not counting the field grown in the background.

method.name: get_runoff_at
method.description: With [member runoff_channels] on, the water running over the ground at [param position]: its depth in metres and speed in m/s. [code]Vector2(0, 0)[/code] where none runs.

method.name: get_runoff_cut_at
method.description: With [member runoff_channels] on, the metres of ground the runoff has cut away at [param position] (negative where it laid sand down), since the field last moved.

method.name: get_runoff_step_usec
method.description: Microseconds the last runoff step took on the CPU (twice a second).

method.name: get_sand_deposit_at
method.description: The wind-blown sand written to the ground at [param position] since that part of the ground came into the field, in m: plants can be buried by it, or grow up through it as marram does.

method.name: get_sand_flux_at
method.description: The saltation flux over [param position], in kg of sand per metre across the wind per second, along the wind (x, z). Open dry sand carries the Lettau and Lettau flux for the wind; it falls to nothing over about a metre among plants.

method.name: get_saturation_at
method.description: The pore water in the top 2 cm of the ground at [param position], as a share of the pore space (0 dry, 1 saturated). See [member water_coupling].

method.name: get_sinkage_at
method.description: How far a body of [param mass] kg on [param area] m² ([param width] m wide, 0: from the area) sinks into the ground at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_standing_water_volume
method.description: The standing water over a disc of [param radius] at [param position] (m³), as last read back from the GPU: what [method add_water] can take there.

method.name: get_step_time_msec
method.description: The time the last physics step took (pressing, slumping, ageing, upload), in milliseconds.

method.name: get_standing_water_at
method.description: The depth of standing water at [param position] in metres (see [member standing_water]), from the latest read back of the GPU field; 0 without one.

method.name: get_surface_height_at
method.description: The printed ground height at [param position]: the undisturbed ground plus the rim minus the dent.

method.name: get_tracked_mud_at
method.description: The tracked mud film at [param position] (see [member tracked_mud]), as last read back: its share of the ground (x, 0 to 1) and its wetness (y, 1 fresh, 0 dried), or [code]Vector2(0, 0)[/code] where there is none. Read at the nearest texel, since the film is stored encoded.

method.name: get_saved_rut_tile_count
method.description: The number of tiles kept on disk in [member ruts_path] for this surface's fields (see [member keep_ruts]).

method.name: get_water_mud_at
method.description: The clay the standing water carries at [param position], kg/m³, as last read back (see [member muddy_water]).

method.name: get_water_added
method.description: The net volume (m³) of the [method add_water] discs applied so far, takes negative.

method.name: get_water_moved
method.description: The water (m³) [method add_water]'s discs put into the main field ([code]x[/code]) and took out of it ([code]y[/code]) so far, as the GPU last read back.

method.name: get_water_owed
method.description: Water (m³) [method add_water]'s takes asked for but did not find, not yet paid back by water added since.

method.name: get_water_speed_at
method.description: The speed of the water flowing over the ground at [param position], m/s; [code]0.0[/code] where it is dry.

method.name: get_water_step_usec
method.description: How long the last water step took, in microseconds (it runs twice a second).

method.name: get_wheel_soil
method.description: The soil under a wheel at [param position]: [param load] N on a wheel of [param radius] and [param width] m, a tyre at [param inflation] kPa ([code]0[/code]: rigid), at [param slip] and [param slip_angle] (radians). Returns [code]soft[/code], [code]static_sinkage[/code], [code]sinkage[/code] (m, with slip sinkage), [code]contact_length[/code] (m), [code]compaction[/code], [code]bulldozing[/code], [code]resistance[/code], [code]shear_limit[/code], [code]traction[/code] and [code]lateral[/code] (N).

method.name: get_wind_step_usec
method.description: The time the last wind step (shelter, flux and deposition, twice a second) took, in microseconds.

method.name: is_gpu_active
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the field runs in compute shaders: [member gpu_simulation] is on and there is a [RenderingDevice] (Forward+ or Mobile).

method.name: is_near_active
method.description: [code]true[/code] when the near field ([member near_field]) is running (it needs the field on the GPU).

method.name: is_ripples_ready
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the first ripple field grown in the background has filled the window.

method.name: mud_viscosity
method.description: The Bingham viscosity of mud, in Pa s, at a volumetric sediment concentration from 0.40 (slurry) to 0.56 (stiff), after O'Brien and Julien (1988).

method.name: mud_yield_stress
method.description: The yield stress of mud, in Pa, at a volumetric sediment concentration from 0.40 (slurry) to 0.56 (stiff), after O'Brien and Julien (1988). Below it mud stands; above it flows.

method.name: press
method.description: Presses the ground down to [param bottom] (world height) under a sphere of [param radius] at [param position] ([param round]) or a flat disc, plus [param sink] below the undisturbed surface. Returns the volume moved, in m³.

method.name: press_box
method.description: Presses a flat print [param size] wide (x) and long (z), turned by [param yaw] about up: a boot, a crate. Returns the volume moved, in m³.

method.name: press_wheel
method.description: Presses a wheel's rut: a flat print [param size] wide (x) and long (z), turned by [param yaw], [param sinkage] m deep, the soil thrown along [param velocity]. Returns the volume moved on the CPU field ([code]0[/code] on the GPU, where it is a stamp).

method.name: refresh_ground
method.description: Samples the height source again (after the terrain changed).

method.name: settle
method.description: Runs slumping and ageing for [param seconds] at once, in steps of [param step].

method.name: shelter_ratio_for
method.description: The share of the wind's friction speed left on the sand among plants of frontal area index [param lambda] (plant frontal area per ground area, clamped to 0.5), by Raupach's 1993 drag partition: 1 on open ground, about 0.22 at marram's 0.3, which stops saltation in any gale.

method.name: sync_deformation
method.description: On the GPU path, waits for the field and reads it back now, so [method get_dent_at], [method get_rim_at], [method get_fresh_at], [method get_surface_height_at] and [method get_moved_volume] show everything pressed so far. It stalls the GPU: for tests and tools, not every frame. Does nothing on the CPU path.

method.name: take_sprays
method.description: The sand thrown by spinning wheels since the last call (from [PhysXVehicle3D] on soft soil), as Dictionaries: [code]position[/code], [code]velocity[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]slip_speed[/code], [code]reach_center[/code] and [code]reach_radius[/code] (the loose sand the tread reaches). Taken by a [PhysXGroundGrains3D]; with none, they are dropped after a couple of physics frames.

method.name: save_ruts
method.description: Writes the tiles the fields hold now to [member ruts_path] (see [member keep_ruts]). Called when the node leaves the tree; call it with the game's own save.

method.name: track_mud
method.description: Presses a film of mud [param depth] m thick over a disc of [param radius] at [param position] onto firm ground (a tyre or boot coming out of the mud, see [member tracked_mud]). A film under a millimetre covers the ground in patches, by its share. [param wet] is how wet it is laid (1 fresh). Returns the volume laid, m³.

method.name: stir_water
method.description: Stirs [param mass] kg of the bed's clay into the standing water over a disc of [param radius] at [param position] (a boot through a puddle, a clod landing in it), where the bed is cohesive (see [member muddy_water]). Applied by the next water step on the GPU.

members.member: The contact area of a [CharacterBody3D] in [member deform_groups] without a [code]ground_contact_area[/code] meta, in m² (one boot by default).
The mass of a [CharacterBody3D] in [member deform_groups] without a [code]ground_mass[/code] meta, in kg.
How close a body's underside must come to the surface to press it, in metres.
A [code]TerrainDataMap3D[/code] whose wetness index, slope and distance to water place mud by themselves ([member mud_auto_depth]). Empty: the height source, when it is one.
The width of the field, in metres. Prints are made only where the terrain is fully lowered: [member terrain_margin] plus [member skirt_fade] inside its edge.

Groups whose nodes press the ground. A node's first collision shape gives its footprint; rigid bodies press by their mass, characters by [member character_mass], others only to their underside. The metas [code]ground_mass[/code], [code]ground_contact_area[/code] and [code]ground_radius[/code] (or the snow ones) override. A [BoxShape3D] with the meta [code]ground_sole[/code] set prints a boot sole (heel, waist, toe and lug tread, the toe toward the box's longer side) instead of a block.
Texels across the field (a multiple of 64).

If [code]true[/code], clay soaked by standing water dries once the ground round it is dry, goes matte, then cracks into plates about four times as wide as its drying layer (about 12 cm), primary cracks first and finer ones splitting the plates, their rims curling up. Rain closes them; each wetting and drying makes the next pattern more regular, towards hexagons. Sand, litter and rock do not crack. Drawn as geometry where the mesh is fine enough, in both renderers.
The patch's vertex spacing over the middle half of the field, in metres.
How long freshly turned ground takes to dry to a third of its darkening, in seconds.

The dust a tyre lifts from fully dry, bare sand, in kilograms per second per metre of tyre width per metre per second of speed (sliding counts twice). Scaled by how much of the ground the wind could move there; damp sand gives none. Carried by a [GroundDust3D].
The node the field follows; the camera when empty.

Runs the field (pressing, slumping, ageing, the turned-ground tint and the tile cache) in compute shaders where there is a [RenderingDevice]; the texture the ground materials sample is written there directly. The queries use a copy read back at 15 Hz. Off, or on the Compatibility renderer, the field runs on the CPU. Turning it over starts the field empty.
The physics layers a downward ray finds the ground on when [member height_source] gives no height.
The spacing of the ground lattice sampled from the height source, in metres.
The ground where [member type_map] says nothing: sand or soil.

The terrain: a [code]TerrainDeformer3D[/code], a baked [code]TerrainDataMap3D[/code], a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], anything with [code]get_height(position)[/code] or Terrain3D. Empty: a downward ray on [member ground_collision_mask].
The canopy closure that drops leaf litter when there is no weather map, from 0 to 1.
The leaf litter under a closed canopy, in metres; less under a thinner one.

The terrain's material. The patch is drawn with a copy of it; turn on [member BaseMaterial3D.ground_deform_enabled] on the original (or call the shader code from a [ShaderMaterial]) so the terrain is lowered under the patch. Map it by world position so the two line up.
How many tiles of prints are kept after the field leaves them.
The ground's moisture from 0 (dry) to 1 (soaked); -1 takes the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wetness.

The mud layer's depth where water gathers by itself, in metres: valley floors, hollows and flats below slopes (a high topographic wetness index) and the first metres of a bank, on ground under about 10 degrees. Needs [member data_map].

Deep mud: where the ground is wet, a soft layer of clay and silt over the firm base, as deep as [member mud_map] and the rules of [member mud_auto_depth] give. It flows as a Bingham fluid (stiff mud holds a rut, slurry closes it), bears and grips as clay, and lets wheels sink to the base.
A painted mud depth over [member mud_map_rect]: the red channel times [member mud_max_depth].
The world rectangle (x, z, width, depth) [member mud_map] covers.
The clay's colour. A [PhysXVehicle3D] that drives through the mud carries it on its tyres and body, so red laterite gives red mud and grey clay grey.
The clay's colour over [member mud_map_rect] (RGB), where it varies; outside it, [member mud_color].
The mud depth where [member mud_map] is white, in metres.
The moisture at which the mud layer reaches its full depth.
The moisture where the ground starts turning to mud. Mud is stiff (a solid share of 0.56) at a moisture of 0.35 and slurry (0.40) soaked.
The near field's side, in metres, centred on the field. A multiple of twice the [member detail_spacing], so the patch's fine ring lines up with its grid.

A finer field in the middle of the deformation field ([member near_extent] at [member near_resolution] texels, by default 8 m at 1.5625 cm against 6.25 cm), pressed and slumped with the same rules and used inside its square by the material and the path tracer, so tread, boot and rill edges are sharp geometry. The patch gains a matching fine ring. Tiles it has never held start from the main field. Needs [member gpu_simulation].
The near field's texels per side (a multiple of 64).
The patch's vertex spacing over the outer half of the field, in metres.
Rigid bodies in [member deform_groups] moving through soft ground feel its resistance: compaction and bulldozing of the soil they move into, at their width.
How fast rain softens prints: the share lost per hour per mm/h of rain.

Width of the square of real ripple geometry round the follow point, m. The patch's middle is meshed at the ripple cell over it, so its vertex count grows as its square (4 m: about 100,000 vertices). The ripples fade out over its outer 15%, into the same field drawn as surface detail (a normal, no shadows of their own) over the rest of the patch.
Speeds up the ripples' growth over real time; [code]1.0[/code] is real time, when ripples take minutes to re-form. For scenes and time-lapses.
If [code]true[/code] and the height source is a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], bare rock (exposure over one half) does not print.

If [code]true[/code], water runs over the ground and cuts it: soaked sand on a slope seeps where the water table a falling tide or a lake left still meets the surface, and rain runs off where the ground cannot take it. The water gathers downhill into sheets and rills, carries sand and lays it down where it slows and at the water's edge, so a beach face grows the branching rills of low tide. It also keeps the sand above a high water table soaked through its capillary fringe. Reads the [member water_sources] and the weather map's rain.
Speeds up the runoff's cutting and the water table's fall, for previews and benches.
How fast wind fills dry sand prints: the share lost per hour at 10 m/s, from nothing at 5 m/s (Bagnold's threshold).

If [code]true[/code], loose dry sand shows its grains up close: their mixed colours, averaging out with distance, and the clean faces among them flashing where they mirror the sun (counted per pixel footprint like snow's sparkle), in raster and under the path tracer alike. Wet sand loses them.

If [code]true[/code], water stands in ruts and prints: rain the ground cannot take, and ground water where a print reaches below the water table (soaked ground has it at the surface), run downhill over the printed ground and gather level in its hollows, then soak in and evaporate. The water is the surface there in both renderers: flat, smooth and murky with the clay it carries, and it softens the mud under it. Needs the GPU field ([member gpu_simulation]). [member runoff_time_scale] speeds up its rain, soaking and evaporation.

If [code]true[/code], the standing water carries clay: tyres rolling on a soft clay bed under it churn a couple of millimetres of slurry into the water as they pass, feet and landing clods stir more in ([method stir_water]), the flow carries it, it settles out at a silt floc's speed (0.1 mm/s, so a stirred puddle clears over minutes) and drying leaves it on the bed. Sand beds leave the water clear. Both renderers draw the water by its clay: the bed hidden within a millimetre or so and the water milky brown with the ground's colour past some tens of kg/m³. Water thrown up carries it ([method get_water_mud_at]), so tyre sheets fly brown and stain what they hit.
How far the terrain is lowered under the patch, in metres.
Over how many metres the lowering reaches its full depth, past [member terrain_margin].
A [code]SnowCover3D[/code]: where it has more than 3 cm of snow, the snow surface takes the print instead.
How far inside the field's edge the terrain starts to be lowered, in metres; at least the terrain's vertex spacing, so no lowered triangle reaches past the patch.

If [code]true[/code], ruts are kept across the world: each 64-texel tile with prints, its dent, rim, tint and standing water, is written to [member ruts_path] as the field moves off it and read back when the field returns, in this session or the next, so the ground stays as it was left. One small zstd file per tile, per field (the main and near fields keep their own); a tile flattened again loses its file. Not used in the editor. Give each surface its own [member ruts_path], and one per save slot.
The folder the kept ruts go to (see [member keep_ruts]).

If [code]true[/code], mud carried out onto firm ground is left on it ([method track_mud]): a vehicle's clogged tread presses part of its clay down as it rolls (most at a crawl, little at a spin, where it flies instead), and boots leave heel and forefoot prints that fade over a dozen steps as the soles come clean. The film darkens the ground while wet, dries in place to the clay's pale tone, is kept by later tyre and foot presses, and is washed off by standing water or dug away. Both renderers draw it.
A map of the ground over [member type_map_rect]: red is the share of sand, green over one half is bare rock.
The world XZ rectangle [member type_map] covers.

If [code]true[/code], water over the ground changes it. Water from [member water_sources] and the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] contact wetness fills the pores of the top layer (saturated in about 10 s under water), which drain to field capacity in a minute or two and dry over hours. Damp sand is firm and holds steep walls; saturated sand slumps as dry sand does. Water flowing faster than the Shields threshold (about 0.25 m/s) moves the sand ([method bed_load]): prints under the swash or a stream are rounded off within a minute, the volume kept. The pore water also shows: wet sand darkens and turns smoother (Lagarde's porous wet surfaces), and a film stands glossy on saturated sand and under the water, in raster and under the path tracer alike, through the [code]ground_wet_map[/code] shader global.

The water nodes the ground reads, sampled on a 1 m grid twice a second: any node with [code]sample_depth(position)[/code] (or [code]sample_height(position)[/code]), [code]sample_flow(position)[/code] and, for a sea's swash, [code]sample_swash(position)[/code], such as the water surface, river and live water nodes.
The 10 m wind over the ground in m/s, as world XZ. [code]Vector2(0, 0)[/code] reads it from the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code].

If [code]true[/code], wind over dry sand grows ripples (Nishimori and Ouchi 1993) over [member ripple_extent] round the follow point: about 11 cm apart and 6 mm high at 8 m/s, crests across the wind, none under about 6 m/s (Bagnold's threshold), on damp sand or under litter (damp sand keeps the ripples it has). Prints wipe them and they grow back; a wind shift turns them. The patch's middle is meshed at the ripple cell, so the crests are real geometry the path tracer sees. [GroundStreamers3D] draws the grains in the air. Off by default until its cost is measured.

Nodes whose plants shelter the sand from the wind, such as a vegetation field: any node with [code]sample_lateral_cover(position)[/code] returning the frontal area index there (0 bare; about 0.05 to 0.3 for dune grass), sampled on a 1 m grid twice a second on the main thread. Sheltered sand moves less (ripples, streamers, prints filled), and sand blown in drops among the plants and builds mounds round them ([method get_deposition_rate_at]).

constants.constant: Sand: dry it caves in to dishes, damp it keeps sharp walls.
Soil: firm when dry, mud when wet.
